name: Traffic Yellow
lede: Traffic Yellow is a brilliant orange-yellow from the German RAL signage standard, built to read as an accent, not a field color.

sections.title: A signal yellow
sections.body:
RAL, founded in 1927, lists this hue as RAL 1023, a screen approximation of that spec [1]. The books give no account of why this particular shade was chosen for signage over a purer yellow, so that design choice is undocumented here [1].

Its nearest named neighbor in our library is [[amber]], just slightly less orange [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
Our archive finds this hue, as photographed, in 71 of 23,781 paintings (0.3 percent), more common than 56 percent of the named colors we track [2]. It peaks in the 1900s, in 7 of 1,674 paintings, at 1.4 times the expected rate for paintings from that century [2]. Inside a painting it most often plays an accent, in 86 percent of its 84 occurrences[2].

[[painter:george-dawe|George Dawe]] is its most devoted painter here, carrying it in 5 of 50 of his works, 7.6 times his home museums' baseline [2]. It is most over-represented in paintings from India, at 4.0 times the expected rate [2]. The earliest matching painting is dated 1400, 527 years before RAL recorded the standard in 1927, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2].

origin.named_after: its use on traffic signs and road markings
